# `notice` commands

## `notice dismiss`

Set a ready notice aside without sending it, with a note saying why. It stays on the record as dismissed, and no new notice is generated for that customer until the next notice period.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | customer |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/notice.dismiss` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow notice dismiss 01JNOTICE00000000000000000 --note "Called; paying Friday" --company "Demo Plumbing Co"`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "notice dismiss", "input": {"notice": "01JNOTICE00000000000000000", "note": "Called; paying Friday"}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

## `notice generate`

Generate overdue notices now, by the company's overdue notice preferences -- what the scheduler in `bookflow serve` does by itself on the notice schedule. One notice per customer or job whose open invoices and statement charges at least `overdue_notice_days` past due total at least the minimum (and whose whole balance is above zero), for this period of the schedule (the month, or the week from Monday). A customer that already has an unreversed notice for the period -- ready, sent or dismissed -- gets no second one. Nothing is sent: each notice waits in `notice list` with a printable statement or letter (`print_path`). The output names its batch; batch reverse dismisses its ready notices and releases their periods. A notice already sent blocks reversal: sent mail cannot be recalled.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | customer |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/notice.generate` |
| External binary body | none |

`bookflow notice generate --as-of 2026-11-01 --reason "Monthly collection notices" --company "Demo Plumbing Co"`


## `notice list`

List overdue notices: ready to send by default, or sent, dismissed or all. Each carries the customer, the overdue balance and documents captured when it was generated, the letter text, and `print_path`, the printable PDF (the customer statement, or the letter). Bookflow never sends a notice itself.

|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | read |
| Required role | member |
| Capability | customer |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/notice.list` |

## `notice reverse`

| `period_released` | boolean | no | no | false | True when reversal released this period for a corrected generation run. |

### Errors

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `E_COMPANY_AMBIGUOUS` | More than one company matches; use the id or Organization/Company. |
| `E_COMPANY_NOT_FOUND` | No such company. |
| `E_CONFIG_INVALID` | The configuration file could not be read. |
| `E_CONTEXT_IN_INPUT` | Input contains a context field. |
| `E_DB_BUSY` | Another Bookflow command is running on this data root. |
| `E_FEATURE_DISABLED` | This feature is not enabled for the company. |
| `E_FS_UNKNOWN` | The filesystem type of the path could not be determined. |
| `E_GUARD_REFUSED` | Bookflow's own safety check in the database refused this write, so nothing was saved. This is a Bookflow bug, not a problem with your input or your disk: please report it with this error's details and request id. |
| `E_INTERNAL` | Internal failure. |
| `E_IO` | A filesystem operation failed. |
| `E_MIGRATION_FAILED` | A schema migration failed; the database was backed up first and is unchanged. |
| `E_NETWORK_SHARE` | The path is on a network filesystem, which Bookflow refuses to use. |
| `E_NOT_INITIALIZED` | The data root is not initialized; run `bookflow init`. |
| `E_NO_ACTOR` | This login is not mapped to a Bookflow user. |
| `E_ORGANIZATION_NOT_FOUND` | No such organization. |
| `E_PARTIAL_WRITE` | The authoritative write committed, but a secondary update remains incomplete. |
| `E_PERMISSION` | The acting user may not run this command here. |
| `E_REASON_REQUIRED` | This write needs a reason: a short phrase naming what triggered it (--reason on the CLI, a top-level reason on MCP, the X-Bookflow-Reason header on HTTP). |
| `E_RECORD_NOT_FOUND` | No such record. |
| `E_SCHEMA_BEHIND` | The database schema is behind this version of Bookflow; run `bookflow upgrade`. |
| `E_SCHEMA_UNKNOWN` | The database schema revision is not known to this version of Bookflow; upgrade Bookflow. |
| `E_UNAUTHENTICATED` | No valid credential: log in, or send a bearer token. |
| `E_USAGE` | Invalid command syntax. |
| `E_VALIDATION` | Invalid input. |
